purpose: Public literature curation and falsifiable preclinical prioritization; no patient data, experiments or efficacy estimates.

sources.title: Molecular Causes for BUBR1 Dysfunction in the Human Cancer Predisposition Syndrome Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy
sources.evidence_access: full text
sources.observation: Checkpoint response recovered with wild-type complementation and abundance restoration for selected unstable mutants; stable alleles could separate checkpoint and alignment functions.
sources.limitation: Allele selection and transformed cells limit transfer; HSP90 inhibition destabilized mutants. No therapeutic drug rescue established.

sources.title: BubR1 allelic effects drive phenotypic heterogeneity in mosaic-variegated aneuploidy progeria syndrome
sources.evidence_access: full text
sources.observation: Similar protein reductions accompanied distinct phenotypes; some muscle phenotypes correlated with mTORC1 hyperactivity.
sources.limitation: Species and allele effects; no mTOR-drug rescue demonstrated. Correction concerns Figure 2E lymphoma image/method; this review does not use that panel.

sources.title: Integration of Kinase and Phosphatase Activities by BUBR1 Ensures Formation of Stable Kinetochore-Microtubule Attachments
sources.evidence_access: full text
sources.observation: KARD phosphorylation promoted PP2A-B56 recruitment and attachments; inhibiting Aurora B reverted the attachment defect.
sources.limitation: Engineered cellular attachment endpoint; not demonstration of safe long-term segregation rescue. Global phosphatase or kinase modulation is not equivalent to local balanced recruitment.

sources.title: BUBR1 Pseudokinase Domain Promotes Kinetochore PP2A-B56 Recruitment, Spindle Checkpoint Silencing, and Chromosome Alignment
sources.evidence_access: full text
sources.observation: Perturbations impaired KARD phosphorylation, PP2A recruitment and checkpoint silencing; chromosome alignment errors increased.
sources.limitation: A structural/regulatory domain contribution complicates claims of kinase-domain dispensability; engineered constructs and expression levels limit allele extrapolation.

sources.title: SIRT2 induces the checkpoint kinase BubR1 to increase lifespan
sources.evidence_access: abstract
sources.observation: Abstract reports increased BubR1 abundance with SIRT2 overexpression or NMN; SIRT2 overexpression increased median survival, more strongly in males.
sources.limitation: Only abstract/synopsis inspected; NMN abundance result must not be called NMN survival or human mutant rescue. Exposure bridge unresolved.

sources.title: Increased expression of BubR1 protects against aneuploidy and cancer and extends healthy lifespan
sources.evidence_access: abstract
sources.observation: Reported genomic protection and reduced tumorigenesis; original figure legend reports correction of hypomorphic growth/aging phenotypes.
sources.limitation: Genetic overexpression is not pharmacological stabilization of mutant protein; complete methods were not accessible.

sources.title: Clearance of p16Ink4a-positive senescent cells delays ageing-associated disorders
sources.evidence_access: abstract
sources.observation: Removal of p16-positive cells delayed selected tissue deterioration; later clearance attenuated progression.
sources.limitation: Requires engineered transgene; not proof for a conventional senolytic, chromosome correction or developmental reversal.

sources.title: P53 independent pathogenic mechanisms contribute to BubR1 microcephaly
sources.evidence_access: full text
sources.observation: DNA damage and residual cell death persisted; later cortical and neuronal rescue was limited and varied by endpoint.
sources.limitation: Near-complete developmental loss differs from partial deficiency; DNA-damage origin remains unresolved. Downstream suppression did not provide broad rescue.

sources.title: Biallelic TRIP13 mutations predispose to Wilms tumor and chromosome missegregation
sources.evidence_access: full text
sources.observation: Restoring TRIP13 rescued chromosome instability and checkpoint defects in deficient cells.
sources.limitation: Alternative etiology evidence only; no alternative finding asserted for the current hypothesis and no BUB1B-drug rescue.

sources.title: MTOR regulates the pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype by promoting IL1A translation
sources.evidence_access: Full primary PDF via author institution; relevant text and figure legends inspected
sources.observation: Reduced IL1A translation and SASP; Figure 6 separates secretory suppression from persistent senescence arrest.
sources.limitation: No segregation rescue or BUB1B disease-model rescue established.

sources.title: Rapamune EPAR and product information
sources.evidence_access: Current EMA EPAR webpage and full product information PDF
sources.observation: EU authorization: specified renal transplantation prophylaxis and sporadic LAM; EPAR updated 2026-06-04.
sources.limitation: Approval is not for BUB1B disease; adult transplant exposure includes co-medication context.

sources.title: Rapamune US prescribing information (2020 archived FDA label)
sources.evidence_access: Full FDA label PDF
sources.observation: Approximately 92% plasma protein binding; blood/plasma ratio 36 ±18.
sources.limitation: Archived label used for PK, not sole proof of current approval; whole blood cannot stand for unbound target-tissue concentration.

sources.title: Metformin hydrochloride tablet US DailyMed label
sources.evidence_access: Full DailyMed label, updated 2025-07-01; sections 1 and 12.3 inspected
sources.observation: Type 2 diabetes glycemic-control indication in adults and children age 10+; usual steady-state plasma <1 microgram/mL; negligible protein binding.
sources.limitation: No BUB1B indication. Not a tissue concentration or universal exposure ceiling.

sources.title: Metformin inhibits the senescence-associated secretory phenotype by interfering with IKK/NF-kappaB activation
sources.evidence_access: Full primary PDF at author institution, Figure 2 and methods inspected
sources.observation: Figure 2 cytokine transcript suppression at 1, 2.5 and 5 mM, with proliferation-marker control.
sources.limitation: Nominal millimolar exposure does not bridge to usual human plasma; not BUB1B rescue.

sources.title: Metformin improves healthspan and lifespan in mice
sources.evidence_access: Primary PMC full text
sources.observation: Lower exposure extended mean lifespan in C57BL/6; measured serum 0.45 ±0.09 mM. Higher exposure shortened mean lifespan.
sources.limitation: Species/exposure mismatch; 5.03 ±0.87 mM serum at toxic higher intervention. Liver nmol/mg protein is not plasma molarity.

sources.title: SPRYCEL US prescribing information
sources.evidence_access: Full current manufacturer US prescribing information including FDA-approved labeling
sources.observation: Approved specified Ph+ CML/ALL uses; plasma Cmax 82.2 ng/mL; 96% plasma binding; half-life 3-5 hours.
sources.limitation: Cancer approval does not validate senolysis. Serious hematologic, pulmonary and developmental liabilities; free estimate extrapolates binding measured at 100-500 ng/mL.

sources.title: The Achilles’ heel of senescent cells: from transcriptome to senolytic drugs
sources.evidence_access: Full primary Wiley article, results and figure material inspected
sources.observation: At least 50 nM dasatinib reduced senescent preadipocyte viability over 3 days; cell-type-dependent response.
sources.limitation: Not BubR1 model; killing rather than segregation correction; combination results cannot be assigned to monotherapy.

sources.title: Small-molecule inhibition of aging-associated chromosomal instability delays cellular senescence
sources.evidence_access: Full primary PMC article and figure legends
sources.observation: 1 micromolar improved aged-fibroblast segregation readouts.
sources.limitation: Higher than 0.1 micromolar could fail or worsen CIN in cancer cells; no verified market approval; not BUB1B rescue.

sources.title: ACETADOTE (acetylcysteine) US prescribing information
sources.evidence_access: Full FDA PDF, indication and section 12.3 inspected
sources.observation: Approved acetaminophen-overdose antidote; total terminal half-life 5.6 h; binding 66-87%; molecular weight 163.2.
sources.limitation: No chronic chromosome-instability indication; binding does not identify reduced-parent target-tissue exposure.

sources.title: Sod1 deficiency in mouse oocytes during in vitro maturation increases chromosome segregation errors with a reduced BUBR1 at kinetochore
sources.evidence_access: Primary PubMed/PMC search excerpts; publisher landing page, subsequent detail requests timed out
sources.observation: Primary abstract/search excerpts report fewer segregation errors with 500 micromolar NAC.
sources.limitation: Different genotype and meiosis; detailed full text unstable; no NAC-to-BUBR1-localization rescue claim extracted.

sources.title: The disposition and kinetics of intravenous N-acetylcysteine in patients with paracetamol overdosage
sources.evidence_access: Full primary abstract inspected
sources.observation: Mean total-plasma early peak 554 mg/L; approximately 35 mg/L after 12 h.
sources.limitation: Historical acute poisoning, transient total concentration, not free reduced NAC or sustained tissue exposure; no chronic-use extrapolation. Primary abstract links adverse reactions to early high concentrations; peak is not a tolerability benchmark.

sources.title: Pharmacokinetics and bioavailability of reduced and oxidized N-acetylcysteine
sources.evidence_access: Primary publisher abstract inspected; full text subscription only
sources.observation: Reduced oral bioavailability 4.0%; total 9.1%; reduced intravenous terminal half-life 1.95 h versus total 5.58 h.
sources.limitation: Small study; no chromosome-instability endpoint or relevant tissue measurements; reduced and total analytes not interchangeable.

sources.title: Oxidative stress induces chromosomal instability through replication stress in fibroblasts from aged mice
sources.evidence_access: full text, Fig4/Fig6 and drug-treatment methods inspected
sources.observation: At 5 mM NAC, aged-cell live imaging showed fewer segregation errors and reduced replication-stress readouts; young-cell response differed.
sources.limitation: Related aging model, not MVA. Millimolar culture exposure; human unbound tissue exposure not established. NAC plus MitoQ/UMK57 did not uniformly add benefit.

sources.title: Contribution of BubR1 to oxidative stress-induced aneuploidy in p53-deficient cells
sources.evidence_access: full text, results and Fig1-3 inspected
sources.observation: NAC prevented oxidant-associated loss of BubR1/Mad2 expression; the paper demonstrates context-dependent p53/BubR1 effects on polyploidy.
sources.limitation: No inherited BUB1B-mutant rescue. Protein preservation is not corrected segregation. p53 modulation must not be inferred to be therapeutic.

sources.title: p21 Both Attenuates and Drives Senescence and Aging in BubR1 Progeroid Mice
sources.evidence_access: PMC full text accessed; results and survival figure legends examined.
sources.observation: Median survival shortened about 35%; p21 protected muscle/fat but promoted lens pathology.
sources.limitation: Tissue-specific opposing effects disfavor indiscriminate senescence suppression. Genetic lifelong loss is not equivalent to transient drug inhibition.

sources.title: Elevating the frequency of chromosome mis-segregation as a strategy to kill tumor cells
sources.evidence_access: Extensive primary PMC indexed results text and PNAS/PubMed bibliographic metadata; direct PMC open blocked.
sources.observation: Increased severe chromosome errors and reduced long-term viability; early survival can miss later death after divisions.
sources.limitation: Cancer-cell killing has opposite intent from preserving constitutionally deficient normal tissue; no correction or treatment-safety inference.

sources.title: Organizer clarification: combinations and investigational drugs
sources.evidence_access: Public discussion; organizer response read in full
sources.observation: Combinations of market-approved drugs permitted with individual and combination rationale; investigational drugs outside current Track 2 scope.
sources.limitation: Does not endorse any particular drug or combination; invitation to raise exceptions is not an exception.

sources.title: Official Track 2 submission instructions and validation
sources.evidence_access: Public source read in full via web
sources.observation: PDF/Markdown report with mechanism; GitHub reproducible code/configs; 3-minute YouTube/Vimeo pitch; latest entry reviewed; one submitting teammate; record AI provider/tier/settings. Repository public after close.
sources.limitation: Source is a mutable main branch; a script/storyboard is not the required recorded video.

sources.title: Official Rules
sources.evidence_access: Public source read in full using read-only HTTPS after web fetch failure
sources.observation: No gated-data redistribution or recontact; deletion within 30 days including intermediate datasets; email cnb@sagebase.org confirmation. Report/repository/video required. CC-BY submissions, attribution, embargo, acknowledgement, privacy and dataset-citation requirements.
sources.limitation: General derived-output sharing permission does not override privacy or gated-data prohibition. This review accepts no terms and verifies no participant eligibility.

sources.title: Official overview and timeline
sources.evidence_access: Public source read in full using read-only HTTPS
sources.observation: Deadline October 24 23:59 UTC. Approved-drug hypotheses for follow-up, not efficacy evidence. Weights 35% rigor, 25% impact, 25% innovation, 15% scalability; judging through December 17 and announcement December 18.
sources.limitation: Dates explicitly subject to change; weights are competition criteria, not calibrated therapeutic probabilities.

sources.title: Official FAQ
sources.evidence_access: Public source read in full using read-only HTTPS
sources.observation: Three Track 2 submissions per team; latest reviewed. GitHub public after close; underlying data gated, results/code/reports CC BY 4.0.
sources.limitation: Not independent corroboration of rules: same organizer and same source repository.

sources.title: Organizer privacy clarification and later consumer-tier correction
sources.evidence_access: Public discussion read in full including final correction
sources.observation: Processor terms require no training/rights and limited-purpose retention; preserve findings, delete genome-carrying files and logs. Final organizer correction permits consumer tiers with training opt-out, no feedback and no safety-review flag; document tier/settings.
sources.limitation: Cannot infer actual account settings or guarantee safety flags. Public-only review does not validate prior controlled-data processing; latest correction supersedes earlier Business/API-only reply.

sources.title: Official current app announcement
sources.evidence_access: Public source read in full using read-only HTTPS
sources.observation: Current banner repeats October 24 23:59 UTC closing time and links discussion 28.
sources.limitation: Linked discussion 28 was inaccessible through web tool and was not relied on.

sources.title: Official repository revision listing
sources.evidence_access: Public tree listing read
sources.observation: Listing displayed main revision 60e1c30 and tabs revision 22726e3.
sources.limitation: Short displayed hashes only; source fetched at mutable main, not cryptographically frozen snapshot.

claims.model: Aged mouse fibroblasts; Sod1-null mouse oocytes
claims.transfer_assumption: A removable stress component exists in the BUB1B model. These are different genotypes and mitosis/meiosis contexts.
claims.falsifier: No per-division benefit when stress and exposure are measured.

claims.transfer_assumption: Oxidative stress is a causal mediator, not only an associated marker.
claims.falsifier: No elevated stress or no segregation improvement after stress normalization.

claims.to_node: Preserved viable lineage output with fewer new errors
claims.transfer_assumption: Relevant analyte, duration and tissue exposure can be attained.
claims.falsifier: Benefit restricted to high nominal exposure, arrest, selective death or probe interference.

claims.transfer_assumption: Direct checkpoint restoration is not assumed.
claims.falsifier: Persistent checkpoint defects despite a redox change.

claims.transfer_assumption: Allele and tissue context transfer only after direct measurement.
claims.falsifier: No elevated mTORC1 signaling in relevant model.

claims.model: Senescent human fibroblasts unrelated to BUB1B
claims.transfer_assumption: Suppressed secretory activity is harmful-state reversal, not merely a biomarker.
claims.falsifier: Target engagement without reduced conditioned-medium harm.

claims.transfer_assumption: Genetic cell-clearance evidence does not establish pharmacological secretory modulation.
claims.falsifier: No functional gain or impaired healthy-cell/progenitor output.

claims.transfer_assumption: Whole-blood concentration cannot substitute for unbound tissue exposure.

claims.falsifier: Errors unchanged or increased despite reduced cytokines.

claims.transfer_assumption: High nominal culture activity transfers to plausible tissue exposure.
claims.falsifier: Effect absent at measured exposure-matched concentrations.

claims.transfer_assumption: Transporter-dependent accumulation is measured, not assumed.
claims.falsifier: Benefit appears only in millimolar positive-control conditions.

claims.transfer_assumption: Selective killing must preserve healthy progenitors and not be called correction.
claims.falsifier: Nonsenescent-cell loss or no net tissue-function gain.

claims.model: INK-ATTAC genetic elimination in BubR1 hypomorphic mice
claims.transfer_assumption: Genetic transgene-dependent clearance is not dasatinib monotherapy.
claims.falsifier: Drug fails selectivity/function or affects different cell populations.

claims.transfer_assumption: Cancer exposure/tolerability cannot establish chronic constitutional use.
claims.falsifier: Depletion, toxicity, genomic selection, or no benefit.

hypotheses.rationale: First uncertainty-reduction experiment only: direct segregation endpoints in oxidative-stress models; no established BUB1B rescue or exposure bridge.
Distinct downstream compensation experiment only if harmful mTORC1/SASP phenotype exists; not checkpoint correction.
Millimolar SASP experiments have a large nominal exposure mismatch; no segregation rescue.
Selective-cell-elimination comparator, rejected as corrective lead; healthy progenitor depletion and serious toxicity concerns.

exposure_records.matrix: nominal culture / historical total plasma at 12 hours
exposure_records.note: 48-hour culture versus acute poisoning; total, reduced, free and tissue NAC differ. This is a nonclinical nominal ratio, not a safe target.

exposure_records.matrix: nominal culture / historical early mean total-plasma peak
exposure_records.note: Transient acute IV peak; no sustained or chronic safety bridge.

exposure_records.matrix: nominal maturation medium / target-tissue exposure unavailable
exposure_records.note: Different genotype, meiotic process and compartment; exact exposure duration not independently verified.
MW914.2g/mol; 15ng/mL whole blood, adult transplant with co-medication. Blood/plasma partition and protein binding preclude free-tissue comparison.

exposure_records.matrix: nominal culture / upper benchmark total plasma
exposure_records.note: Usual plasma is below1microgram/mL; using metformin free-base MW129.16. Ratio is therefore a lower-bound benchmark, not an intracellular ratio.

exposure_records.matrix: nominal culture / upper benchmark total plasma
exposure_records.note: Same lower-bound interpretation; no unmeasured tissue-accumulation rescue.

exposure_records.matrix: nominal 3-day culture / transient total plasma peak
exposure_records.note: 96%binding gives approximate free peak0.00674uM, not measured tissue exposure; half-life3–5h. Nominal total ratio does not pass exposure gate.
